children: flydubai Holidays is expanding its destination and product portfolio and preparing to launch a refreshed digital experience as demand for travel packages continues to grow.
Beyond logistics, the partnership will focus on addressing one of the key challenges businesses face when looking to expand internationally.
Customers can choose from holiday packages catering to different budgets and travel preferences, with popular destinations including Almaty, Baku, Krabi, the Maldives, Tbilisi, Yerevan and Zanzibar.
flydubai Holidays is also set to introduce a revamped digital platform aimed at improving the customer experience.
The modernised platform will feature improved navigation, clearer content structure, greater mobile responsiveness and enhanced usability, allowing customers to manage their entire holiday on the go.

The upgraded booking journey will also include enhanced search and filtering options, alongside a more intuitive interface designed to make it easier for customers to curate and manage their holidays according to their preferences and requirements.

Sudhir Sreedharan, Divisional Senior Vice President of Commercial Operations at flydubai, said: “As part of our longstanding commitment to enabling free flows of tourism and passenger connectivity, we are pleased to see continued growth in our holidays division. Through our curated holiday packages, we are giving customers greater choice, flexibility and convenience when planning their holidays, supported by our growing network and a more intuitive, seamless digital experience.

With more than 100 destinations and 10,000 hotels to choose from, customers have access to a wide range of experiences, and we expect this appetite for holiday packages to continue into the upcoming winter season. Customers travelling across our network to Dubai can either take advantage of our stopover experience in the city before exploring the rest of our diverse network.”

Since March 2026, flydubai Holidays has reported a positive response to its Dubai stopover experience, which offers customers exclusive rates on flights, hotels, attractions, activities and services when they choose to stopover in the city.

Nelson D’souza, Vice President of flydubai Holidays, added: “From city breaks to beach holidays, we have seen consistent demand from our customers, particularly across the UAE, GCC and Central Asia, who are increasingly looking beyond established holiday destinations to discover new experiences across Eastern Europe and Asia. There has also been a growing interest in our fixed-package itineraries, as well as premium hotels and services, reflecting a desire among customers to make the most of their holiday and have peace of mind. As we approach the end of the year, we anticipate more customers taking advantage of not only our packages in Dubai, but also in destinations across our network such as Kenya, Tanzania, the Maldives and Thailand.”
Baku, Krabi and Tivat have recorded the strongest growth.

Tivat’s seasonal summer service has been extended until October 23, while Bangkok has become one of the fastest-growing destinations, moving from a daily service launched in July to triple-daily flights from November.
